questions.q: In 2026 the Karnataka High Court permitted a hysterectomy for a woman with severe intellectual disability. The doctrine under which a court acts as guardian of a person who cannot decide for herself is called
questions.e: Under parens patriae, 'parent of the nation', the court steps in to protect the best interests of a person unable to give informed consent, here weighing health, dignity and bodily integrity. Parents and doctors cannot decide such an irreversible procedure on their own. Res judicata bars relitigation of a decided matter, locus standi concerns who may approach a court, and the doctrine of necessity justifies otherwise unlawful action in an emergency.

questions.q:
With reference to the law on reproductive procedures for women with disabilities, consider the following statements:
1. Section 10 of the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016 bars any procedure leading to infertility without the person's free and informed consent.
2. Under the Medical Termination of Pregnancy Act, 1971, the guardian may consent to an abortion on behalf of a woman with intellectual disability.
3. In Suchita Srivastava v. Chandigarh Administration (2009), the Supreme Court upheld the reproductive choice of a woman with mild intellectual disability under Article 21.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. The abortion law draws a distinction: a guardian may consent for a woman with mental illness, but a woman with intellectual disability must still give her own consent, so statement 2 is wrong. In Suchita Srivastava the authorities wanted to end the pregnancy of a rape survivor without her consent; the Court let it continue and asked the State to support mother and child.

questions.q: In Dr Narendra Gupta v. Union of India (2023), the Supreme Court dealt with
o: forced sterilisation targets under the family planning programme
unnecessary hysterectomies performed on vulnerable women
access to abortion beyond 24 weeks of pregnancy
questions.e: The petition exposed hysterectomies done without medical need, often on poor women, sometimes to draw insurance payments. The Court directed all States to follow the health ministry's 2022 guidelines, set up monitoring committees at national, State and district levels and act against hospitals that operate without necessity or informed consent. It treated reproductive rights as part of Article 21.

questions.q:
With reference to the Census, consider the following statements:
1. Before 1951, a temporary Census organisation was set up for each round.
2. The Office of the Registrar General and Census Commissioner functions under the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation.
3. Census 2027 will be the eighth Census after Independence.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. A permanent organisation came after the Census Act, 1948. The Registrar General's office is under the Ministry of Home Affairs, so statement 2 is wrong. Census comes under Entry 69 of the Union List. Census 2027 follows a gap of about fifteen years, will be largely digital with self-enumeration, and will enumerate caste.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: Information given by an individual during the Census cannot be used as evidence against that person in a court or for taxation.
Statement-II: The Census Act, 1948 requires the records of individuals to be kept confidential.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is the correct explanation for Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is not the correct explanation for Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Both statements are correct and the second explains the first. The Act bars disclosure of individual returns, so they cannot be used for law enforcement, tax or other adverse action; only aggregated data are released. This assurance matters more now that Census 2027 lets households enumerate themselves online before the enumerator's visit, while door-to-door enumeration continues in a hybrid model.

questions.q: The reservation of seats for women in the Lok Sabha and State Legislative Assemblies is linked to Census 2027 because
o: the Census will identify the constituencies with the lowest female literacy for reservation
reservation will take effect only after delimitation based on the first Census held after the commencement of the law
the Census will determine the proportion of seats to be reserved
the law requires the Census to record women's political participation first
questions.e: The Constitution (One Hundred and Sixth Amendment) Act, 2023 provides that reservation of one-third of seats comes into force after a delimitation exercise based on the first Census taken after the Act. The Census also feeds delimitation of seats generally, reservation for Scheduled Castes and Tribes, and the Finance Commission's sharing of taxes, which is why it shapes both representation and fiscal federalism.
questions.s: Shankar IAS p. 38; the 2023 amendment is static

questions.q:
With reference to the legal framework against human trafficking in India, consider the following statements:
1. Article 23 of the Constitution prohibits traffic in human beings and begar.
2. Under Section 143 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, the use of force or deception must be shown even when the victim is a child.
3. The Immoral Traffic (Prevention) Act, 1956 was enacted in pursuance of a United Nations convention of 1949.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Section 143 follows the Palermo Protocol's test of act, means and purpose, but for children the 'means' element, such as force, fraud or deception, need not be shown, so statement 2 is wrong. India ratified the 1949 convention on suppression of traffic in 1950 and enacted the 1956 law against trafficking for commercial sexual exploitation.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: According to the Supreme Court, voluntary sex work by adults should not be treated as trafficking.
Statement-II: Under Section 143 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, sexual exploitation amounts to trafficking only when the act, means and purpose elements are all present.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is the correct explanation for Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is not the correct explanation for Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Both statements are correct and the second explains the first. The 1956 law had in effect treated all sex work as trafficking. The newer test, taken from the Palermo Protocol, requires an act such as recruitment or harbouring, a means such as force or deception, and an exploitative purpose. The Court also said sex workers have rights to dignity and safety, irrespective of any 'right to sex work'.

questions.q: The 'Palermo Protocol', to which India is a party, supplements the
o: Convention on the Rights of the Child
UN Convention against Transnational Organized Crime
International Labour Organization's Forced Labour Convention
questions.e: The Protocol to Prevent, Suppress and Punish Trafficking in Persons, especially Women and Children, is one of the protocols to the convention on organised crime. India signed the convention in 2002 and ratified both in May 2011. India is also party to the Convention on the Rights of the Child and its optional protocol on the sale of children, and to the SAARC convention on trafficking of women and children.

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs:
Initiative : Purpose
1. Raksha AI : Mapping vulnerable communities and likely trafficking routes using geospatial data and machine learning
2. Shakti Sadan : Shelter and vocational training for destitute women and trafficking victims
3. Emergency Response Support System : Single pan-India emergency number 112
How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
questions.e: All three pairs are correct. Shakti Sadan is a component of Mission Shakti. Other measures include the Anti Trafficking Cell in the Home Ministry, the extension of the National Investigation Agency's remit to inter-State and cross-border trafficking, Safe City projects and awareness work by the Railway Protection Force and the National Commission for Women at railway stations.

questions.q:
A 'Minimum Universal Disability Pension Floor Rate' was proposed in 2026. Which of the following are cited as its constitutional or legal basis?
1. Article 41 of the Constitution
2. Section 24 of the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016
3. Article 28 of the UN Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.e: Article 41, a Directive Principle, asks the State to make provision for public assistance in cases of disablement; Section 24 of the 2016 Act requires adequate social security; Article 28 of the UN Convention covers an adequate standard of living and social protection. Today disability pensions depend on the State of residence, often Rs 300 to 500 a month, which the proposal calls a postcode lottery.

questions.q:
With reference to the proposal for a national disability pension floor, consider the following statements:
1. India's spending on disability welfare is estimated at about 0.02 per cent of GDP.
2. The Census of 2011 counted about 6 crore persons with disabilities.
3. Even a floor of Rs 15,000 a month is estimated to cost more than one per cent of GDP.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: Only statement 1 is correct. The 2011 Census counted about 2.68 crore persons with disabilities; 4.5 to 6 crore is the present estimate. Statement 3 is wrong: a floor of Rs 8,000 a month for 40 lakh people would cost about Rs 38,400 crore, under 0.1 per cent of GDP, and even Rs 15,000 stays below 0.2 per cent.

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs:
National agency for disability or social security : Country
1. SASSA : South Africa
2. NDIA : Australia
3. INSS : Brazil
How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
questions.e: All three pairs are correct. The South African Social Security Agency runs a national disability grant on uniform norms, Australia's National Disability Insurance Agency runs that country's scheme, and Brazil's national social security institute administers benefits including a minimum income for disabled persons. These single national authorities are the model for the proposed Indian authority. India spends far less on disability as a share of GDP than these countries.

questions.q:
With reference to on-screen marking of Class 12 answer books by the Central Board of Secondary Education in 2026, consider the following statements:
1. Students wrote their answers on a computer instead of on paper.
2. Problems reported included blurred scans, missing pages and some students being shown other candidates' answer books.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Only statement 2 is correct. Students still write on paper; the scripts are scanned, anonymised and sent to evaluators who mark them on screen. The board had considered the system in 2014 but dropped it for want of suitable scanners. The gains claimed are uniformity, no totalling errors and faster results; the concerns are poor reproduction of diagrams and handwriting and the gap between well-equipped and poorly equipped schools.

questions.q: The Union health ministry banned 16 fixed-dose combination drugs in 2026. Under which law are such bans issued?
o: New Drugs and Clinical Trials Rules, 2019
Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act, 1985
questions.e: Section 26A of the 1940 Act lets the Centre prohibit the manufacture, sale or distribution of a drug that is risky or lacks therapeutic justification. The Drugs Technical Advisory Board advises on the merit of combinations, and the Central Drugs Standard Control Organisation, the national regulator, executes. Earlier rounds covered 344 combinations in 2016, 328 in 2018 and 156 in 2024.

questions.q:
With reference to fixed-dose combination drugs, consider the following statements:
1. They contain two or more active ingredients in a fixed ratio in a single dosage form.
2. All fixed-dose combinations are considered irrational by Indian regulators.
3. Unjustified combinations containing antibiotics add to antimicrobial resistance.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Many combinations are rational and widely used, for instance in HIV, tuberculosis, diabetes and hypertension, because they reduce the pill burden and cost, so statement 2 is wrong. The bans target combinations without proven benefit, such as an antibiotic with an anti-inflammatory enzyme, which add side effects, prevent doctors from adjusting doses and drive resistance.

questions.q:
With reference to India's health system, consider the following statements:
1. Public spending on health is above 3 per cent of GDP.
2. Out-of-pocket expenditure is about two-fifths of total health spending.
3. The number of hospital beds per 1,000 people is above the norm suggested by the World Health Organization.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: Only statement 2 is correct; out-of-pocket spending is about 39.4 per cent of total health spending. Public spending is about 1.9 per cent of GDP, so statement 1 is wrong. Statement 3 is wrong: India has about 1.3 beds per 1,000 people against a norm of 2 to 3. The critique is that wellness branding and digital IDs cannot replace curative care.

questions.q:
With reference to sickle cell disease, consider the following statements:
1. It is caused by a mutation in the beta-globin gene on chromosome 11.
2. It is inherited in an autosomal dominant pattern, so one defective gene causes the disease.
3. Sickled red blood cells survive for a much shorter time than normal red blood cells.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. The mutation produces haemoglobin S, which stiffens under low oxygen and deforms cells into sickles that live 10 to 20 days against about 120. Inheritance is autosomal recessive, so statement 2 is wrong: a person with one defective gene is a carrier with the trait, and two are needed for the disease. This is why genetic counselling of carriers is central to the elimination mission.

questions.q:
With reference to the National Sickle Cell Anaemia Elimination Mission, consider the following statements:
1. It aims to eliminate sickle cell disease as a public health problem by 2047.
2. It is implemented jointly by the health ministry and the Ministry of Tribal Affairs.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Both statements are correct. The disease falls heavily on Scheduled Tribe communities, hence the joint role. Over 7 crore people have been screened, about 2.46 lakh patients identified and over 4 crore genetic status cards issued, linked to digital health identities. Sickle cell disease is also listed as a benchmark disability under the 2016 disability law.

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs:
Therapy : Approach
1. Hydroxyurea : Raises the level of foetal haemoglobin
2. Casgevy : Gene editing of the patient's own stem cells using CRISPR
3. Allogeneic bone marrow transplant : Uses the patient's own marrow, so no donor is required
How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
questions.e: Pairs 1 and 2 are correct. Hydroxyurea is a disease-modifying drug, and Casgevy edits the patient's own cells, which removes the need for a matched donor. Pair 3 is wrong: 'allogeneic' means the marrow comes from another person, which is why a donor is needed; that is the limitation gene therapy overcomes. Gene therapy remains unaffordable for most tribal families, an equity concern.

questions.q: World Sickle Cell Day, whose 2026 observance in India was held at Omkareshwar in Madhya Pradesh, is observed every year on
questions.e: The UN General Assembly recognised sickle cell disease as a public health problem in 2008 and designated 19 June for awareness. The 2026 theme centred on closing the survival gap through equitable access to diagnosis and treatment. 24 March is World TB Day, 8 May World Thalassaemia Day and 14 November World Diabetes Day.
questions.s: Shankar IAS p. 143; other days are static

questions.q:
With reference to the PreVenTB trial led by the Indian Council of Medical Research, consider the following statements:
1. It tested two indigenous vaccines, VPM1002 and Immuvac.
2. It is the first trial to evaluate vaccine efficacy against extra-pulmonary tuberculosis.
3. VPM1002 showed close to 100 per cent efficacy in all age groups.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. The trial covered over 12,700 participants at 18 sites. VPM1002 showed about 50 per cent efficacy against extra-pulmonary tuberculosis overall and about 65 per cent in children aged 6 to 14, so statement 3 is wrong. The argument is to use moderately effective vaccines now, alongside nutrition support, preventive therapy and better diagnosis, rather than wait for a perfect vaccine.

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs:
TB vaccine : Developer
1. VPM1002 : Serum Institute of India
2. Immuvac : Bharat Biotech
3. BCG : Indian Council of Medical Research
How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
questions.e: Only pair 1 is correct. VPM1002 is a single-dose recombinant vaccine of the Serum Institute built on BCG. Immuvac, based on Mycobacterium indicus pranii, is from Cadila. BCG was developed by Calmette and Guerin in France about a century ago. India carries about 27 per cent of the world's tuberculosis cases.
questions.s: Shankar IAS pp. 144-145; BCG's origin is static

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: A person with latent tuberculosis infection is highly infectious to others.
Statement-II: In latent infection the bacteria are present but inactive, and the person has no symptoms.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is the correct explanation for Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is not the correct explanation for Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Statement-I is incorrect and Statement-II is correct. In latent infection the bacteria are inactive, the person has no symptoms and is not infectious; it shows only on a skin or blood test. Active disease, especially of the lungs, is what spreads. Preventing progression from latent to active disease is a key goal of vaccines such as Immuvac.

questions.q:
With reference to the sixth National Family Health Survey, consider the following statements:
1. Obesity among women aged 15 to 49 rose to over 30 per cent.
2. The prevalence of high blood sugar among men rose to above 20 per cent.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Both statements are correct. Obesity among women rose to 30.7 per cent and among men to 27.3 per cent, and high blood sugar among men to 20.9 per cent. India now faces a double burden: stunting and thinness among adolescents persist alongside rising overweight. Schools are seen as the key setting, with healthy meals, limits on foods high in fat, sugar and salt, and daily physical activity.

questions.q: The 'thin-fat phenotype', noticed among Indian children and adolescents, refers to individuals who
o: are underweight in childhood and become obese in adulthood
look lean but carry high metabolic risk such as insulin resistance and raised triglycerides
have normal weight but very low muscle strength
are obese but have normal blood sugar and lipid levels
questions.e: Such children have a low body-mass index but relatively more body fat, especially around the abdomen, and less muscle, which gives them a high risk of diabetes and heart disease later. It is one reason why adolescence is treated as the window for preventing non-communicable disease. The rise of ultra-processed food in Indian diets adds to the risk.

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs:
Scheme : Focus
1. Pradhan Mantri Matru Vandana Yojana : Cash incentive to pregnant and lactating women
2. PM POSHAN : Hot cooked meals for children in government schools
3. Anaemia Mukt Bharat : Iron and folic acid supplementation
How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
questions.e: All three pairs are correct. PM POSHAN is the renamed mid-day meal scheme. These sit alongside POSHAN Abhiyaan, which tracks outcomes across ministries, and Anganwadi services for children up to six and for mothers. Suggested additions include attention to the first thousand days, food fortification, biofortified crops and more nutrition rehabilitation centres.

questions.q:
With reference to inflammatory bowel disease, consider the following statements:
1. Crohn's disease is confined to the lining of the colon and rectum.
2. Ulcerative colitis can affect any part of the digestive tract, from the mouth to the anus.
3. Irritable bowel syndrome is a form of inflammatory bowel disease.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: None of the statements is correct; the first two swap the two diseases. Crohn's disease can affect any part of the tract and is patchy, reaching the deeper layers of the gut wall, whereas ulcerative colitis is continuous and limited to the lining of the colon and rectum. Irritable bowel syndrome is a functional disorder without such inflammation.
